column2: Same form in both futures: for είμαι, έχω, ξέρω, κάνω and αρέσω the simple future and the future continuous look the same, because these verbs have no separate aorist stem for the future.
Missing perfect forms (—): είμαι and ξέρω have no present perfect / past perfect. Greek uses other verbs instead (for example, έμαθα for "I came to know").
έρχομαι: the simple past ήρθα and the simple future θα έρθω have active endings, even though the present is passive in form. That is why it sits in the passive group together with γίνομαι.
κάθομαι: the colloquial forms θα κάτσω and έχω κάτσει are also common.

The perfect tenses: they are built with έχω / είχα + the same fixed form (πει, δει, φάει, ...), which does not change with the person. For example: έχω πει, έχεις πει, έχει πει; είχα πει, είχες πει, είχε πει.
είμαι and έχω have no separate aorist, so the same form (ήμουν, είχα) is used for both past tenses.
θέλω: the imperfect ήθελα is used far more often than the aorist θέλησα.
ξέρω: ήξερα means "I knew". For "I found out" or "I learned", use έμαθα.
Many compound verbs follow the verb they come from, for example προσθέτω → πρόσθεσα, and παραλαμβάνω → παρέλαβα, like λαμβάνω.
